name: AUDIT-C
source: WHO (Bush et al., 1998). Free to use.
note: Published cutoff is >=4 for men and >=3 for women. Reitti applies the lower (>=3) threshold for everyone rather than asking for sex at this step; the clinician co-founder owns this decision.

fi.publisher: THL, Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare (AUDIT-C form, 12/2025)
fi.licence: THL (Finnish Institute for Health and Welfare) public form; no form-specific licence printed. The AUDIT is a WHO instrument, free to use. THL's general site terms (text may be quoted with the source acknowledged) could not be re-read at source on this date: the page has moved. Confirm before relying on it.
fi.note: The form has no question stem, so the prompt is empty rather than written by us. Its printed interpretation (women 5+, men 6+, over 65 4+) differs from this app's provisional threshold; that is the clinician's (C10), not part of this change.
